headline_decomposition.question: Of the -61.5% drawdown, how much was multiple compression vs a change in the earnings/FCF base?

log_attribution.plain_english: 158% of the drawdown is multiple compression. The earnings base did not deteriorate at all -- it grew ~75% and OFFSET 58% of the decline. Counterfactual: at an unchanged 68.7x the stock would be $1,201; at FY2021 EPS with today's 15.2x it would be $152.

headline_decomposition.verdict: THE MULTIPLE BROKE, NOT THE BUSINESS -- on every disclosed metric available as of 2026-08-07.

net_new_arr_trend.question: Is net-new ARR still growing? (the single most falsifiable AI-erosion indicator)
net_new_arr_trend.trend_verdict: STILL POSITIVE AND DOLLAR-FLAT. Net-new ARR ran $1.91B / $2.00B / ~$1.98B across FY2023-FY2025 -- no shrinkage. The GROWTH RATE is decelerating monotonically and mildly (12.6% -> 11.5% -> guided 10.2% incl. ~1.9pp of acquired Semrush ARR -> ~8.3% organic), roughly -1 to -1.5pp per year. This is a slope, not a cliff. 'AI killed it' is NOT visible in the numbers. The genuinely adverse fact is not the deceleration -- it is that Adobe retired the metric that would prove or disprove it, twice, exactly as the deceleration became visible.
disclosure_degradation: Through Q4 FY2024: quarterly net-new Digital Media ARR + ending DM ARR + Creative ARR + Document Cloud ARR
FY2025: net-new ARR discontinued; Creative/Document Cloud split discontinued; only ending DM ARR + YoY remained

FY2026: Digital Media ARR discontinued entirely; three reportable segments (Digital Media / Digital Experience / Publishing and Advertising) COMBINED INTO ONE; only Total Adobe ending ARR + YoY remains

module_signals.finding: Financial evidence is excellent and fully primary (SEC 8-K Ex-99.1 for Q2FY26/Q1FY26/Q4FY25/Q4FY24 + FY2025 & FY2021 10-K), with verbatim extracts in raw/. But the competitive side is EMPTY (web search budget exhausted 200/200 this run) and the key operating metric has been retired by the company. Cannot reach +2.

97.0% of Q2 FY26 revenue is subscription; RPO $22.27B; revenue growth ACCELERATED to +12.7% YoY. The revenue machine is healthy and speeding up. But the split between 'professional workflow lock-in' and 'generative-substitutable' revenue is NEVER disclosed, so mechanism durability cannot be evidenced. Also: ARR is an ending-stock metric and revenue is a flow metric, so 'ARR decelerating + revenue accelerating' is consistent with BOTH a benign pricing-cadence story and an adverse churn story -- and this run cannot distinguish them (no NRR, no seat counts, no net-new ARR).

An honest zero. Structural (category-blocking): PDF / ISO 32000, Acrobat's position in compliance and e-signature workflow, embedded Adobe Experience Platform enterprise contracts, and file-format gravity (PSD/AI/PRPROJ) in team pipelines. Merely incumbent (BSX-lesson exposed): standalone image and video GENERATION, template/social design (Canva), and collaborative UI design (Figma). Adobe does not disclose the revenue split across that line, so the module cannot resolve in either direction.

The strongest module. TTM FCF $10.28B on $25.20B revenue = 40.8% FCF margin; capex only 0.8% of revenue (no hyperscaler capex problem); FY2025 beat the TOP END of its own revenue, ARR-growth and non-GAAP EPS guidance; FY2026 revenue and non-GAAP EPS targets RAISED mid-year; diluted share count 481M -> 402M (-16.4%) with buybacks fully covering SBC. The one blemish: FY2025 buybacks were 114% of FCF, turning net cash into $1.02B net debt.

Three adverse structural facts arriving together: (1) metric degradation in two consecutive years, timed with visible ARR deceleration; (2) leadership vacuum -- CEO transition announced 2026-03-12 with no successor named 5 months later, CFO departed 2026-06-15 with an 'interim' replacement still in place; (3) buybacks exceeding FCF. Not a franchise-death signal, but a genuine monitoring/verifiability trap.

Base 10y IRR +14.15% vs the 8% hurdle, with the bear case losing only -2.42%/yr over 10 years. Reverse-solve: at $265.74 with an unchanged 13x exit, the market is pricing owner earnings to compound at just +0.29%/yr for a decade -- i.e. flat forever -- while the company grows revenue 12.7% and guides non-GAAP EPS +16-17%. Price is NOT the binding constraint here.

binding_constraint: COMPLETENESS / VERIFIABILITY -- explicitly NOT price. The base case clears the 8% hurdle by 6pp and the bear case loses only 2.4%/yr; price offers a genuine margin of safety. What caps this dossier is that Adobe retired the single most falsifiable operating metric (net-new Digital Media ARR, then Digital Media ARR itself, then collapsed three reportable segments into one) exactly as ARR growth decelerated from 12.6% to 11.5%, AND is simultaneously operating without a named CEO successor (5 months) or a permanent CFO (2 months). The thesis is currently correct on the numbers and expensive to keep monitoring.

Any of these supports scaling from 3% toward 6%.

runner_dissent: I am using 'no bad news' as 'good news'. Every optimistic conclusion in this card rests on a negative proposition: AI erosion is not visible in the disclosed data. But Adobe removed net-new ARR in FY2025 and removed Digital Media ARR (plus merged three segments into one) in FY2026 -- timed exactly with ARR growth sliding from 12.6% to 11.5%. Management framed it as a shift to customer-group reporting; the effect is that from FY2026 onward, outsiders can no longer verify whether the creative business itself is losing customers. I cannot prove intent, but I must concede: if I ran a slowly bleeding company, this is precisely what I would do. The BSX lesson is that a first mover can go from 100% to 41% share in 2.5 years -- and BSX's share was OBSERVABLE. Adobe's no longer is. Second, ARR is an ending-stock metric and revenue is a trailing flow metric, so 'ARR decelerating while revenue accelerates' is equally consistent with benign pricing cadence and with churn that has not yet hit the P&L; with no NRR, no seat count and no net-new ARR, this run genuinely cannot tell them apart. Third, Adobe is replacing its CEO and CFO simultaneously, in the middle of the attack. That is why initial size is 3% rather than the 5-6% the IRR alone would justify. Against all that: the current price implies owner earnings compound at +0.29%/yr for a decade while the company just RAISED revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance, grew revenue 12.7%, converts 40.8% of revenue to FCF on 0.8% capex intensity, and loses only 2.4%/yr in a harsh bear case. That payoff structure is rare. My STARTER is not because it is insufficiently cheap -- it is because I cannot see half of what I am buying, and the invisible half is the crux. Hence binding_constraint = COMPLETENESS, not PRICE.
